newsitem.title: UK: UK manufacturing output - 0.3 pct in August.
newsitem.headline: UK manufacturing output - 0.3 pct in August.

text.p: The Office for National Statistics (ONS) released the following seasonally adjusted data on UK industrial production in August:
MINING/QUARRYING INCLUDING OIL AND GAS EXTRACTION

NOTE - Consensus forecast was for industrial production to rise by 0.4 percent in August, for a year-on-year rise of 0.9 percent. Manufacturing output was also expected to rise 0.4 percent on the month, but fall 0.1 percent year-on-year.
The ONS said in the three months to August just under half of the manufacturing industries have shown increases in production compared to the previous three months.

Most notable increases were of 2.2 percent in the output of transport equipment industries, 1.0 percent in the output of textiles, clothing and leather industries and 0.6 percent in the output of the pulp, paper, printing and publishing industries.
But there were significant falls of 7.1 percent in the output of coke, mineral oil refining and nuclear fuels industries and 2.9 percent in the output of non-metallic mineral products.

The ONS said output of the durable goods industries fell by 0.2 percent in the three months to August vs the previous three. An increase of 0.6 percent in the output of cars was not enough to offset a fall of 0.9 percent in the output of other durable goods.
Output in the non-durable goods industries rose by 0.4 percent in the latest three months.
Increases of 1.4 percent in clothing and footwear and 0.7 percent in the output of other non-durables more than offset a 0.2 percent fall in the food, drink and tobacco industries.
The ONS said the trend in the manufacturing sector remained flat.
